spacr.ops_prefix.prefix_cell_calls.before:
Each cell's barcode, its read counts and its quality class.

:param reads: one row per read with ``keys``, ``status``, ``key``,
    ``distance``, ``prefix``, ``guide``, ``gene`` and ``level``
    (:func:`match_prefix_reads` joined to the read positions); rows
    whose ``cell`` is 0 are not in a cell.
:param min_reads: exact reads a ``perfect`` cell needs
    (``ops_quality_min_reads``) under ``'spacr'``.
:param keys: the columns naming a cell.
:param method: ``ops_prefix_quality_method``: ``'spacr'``
    (:func:`classify_cell`, classes :data:`QUALITY_CLASSES`) or
    ``'recipe_simple'`` (:func:`recipe_simple_quality` on the exact and
    corrected reads, each scored one minus its distance over the key
    length; classes :data:`RECIPE_SIMPLE_CLASSES`).
:param minority_min_reads: ``ops_prefix_minority_min_reads`` (item 967,
    alpha). From 2 up, a barcode with fewer reads than this is left out
    of the cell's call when another barcode in the cell has strictly
    more reads; tied barcodes still block the call. This rescues cells
    that a single stray read of a second barcode makes ``bad`` under
    ``'recipe_simple'``; under ``'spacr'`` it changes no call and can
    only turn ``great`` into ``perfect``. 0 (the default) and 1 change
    nothing.
:param distance_weight: ``ops_prefix_distance_weight`` (item 988,
    alpha), read only by ``'weighted_majority'``: ``'off'``,
    ``'decay'`` or ``'distance_only'`` (:data:`READ_WEIGHT_MODES`).
    The distance term needs a ``nuc_gap_px`` column, each read's
    distance in pixels to the nucleus of its cell.
:param decay_px: the decay length in pixels
    (``ops_prefix_distance_decay_px``).
:param interior_px: the distance with full weight
    (``ops_prefix_distance_interior_px``).
:param min_weight: the smallest distance term
    (``ops_prefix_distance_min_weight``).
:param weighted_quality: ``ops_prefix_weighted_quality``. True weights
    each read by ``min(1, quality) + 0.05``, and False weights it 1.
:param neighbour_discount: ``ops_read_neighbour_discount``. A barcode
    with strictly fewer reads than the cell's top barcode has its weight
    multiplied by this when it is a top barcode of a touching cell. 1
    is off.
:param weighted_min_share: ``ops_prefix_weighted_min_share``. The share
    of the cell's read weight the top barcode needs.
:param neighbours: the touching cells, needed for a discount below 1.
    The table has the ``keys`` columns, naming a cell, and
    ``neighbour``, the label of a cell it touches in the same site.
:returns: one row per cell with any read: ``keys``, ``reads``,
    ``matched`` (exact or corrected), ``exact``, ``corrected``,
    ``ambiguous``, ``collision``, ``out_of_library``, ``barcodes``
    (distinct callable barcodes), ``prefix``, ``guide``, ``gene`` and
    ``level`` of the top barcode (empty unless ``perfect`` or ``great``),
    ``top_reads``, ``top_exact``, ``top_share`` (of matched reads),
    ``second_reads``, ``has_exact_read`` and ``quality``. With
    ``minority_min_reads`` 2 or more, ``barcodes``, ``second_reads`` and
    the class count only the reads the rule keeps, and two columns are
    added: ``minority_ignored`` (reads left out) and
    ``minority_rescued`` (True when the cell is called only because of
    the rule). Under ``'weighted_majority'`` (:data:`WEIGHTED_CLASSES`)
    the top barcode is the one with the most weight, and five columns
    are added. ``weight_top`` and ``weight_total`` are the summed read
    weights of the top barcode and of the cell. ``d_weight_top`` is the
    summed distance term of the top barcode's reads, and
    ``g_median_top`` their median nucleus distance (NaN without one).
    ``bleed_discounted`` counts the barcodes the neighbour discount
    weighed down.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown method or read-weight mode, for the
    minority-read rule combined with ``'weighted_majority'``, or for a
    discount below 1 without ``neighbours``.

spacr.ops_sbs.neighbour_bleed_flags.source:
Identify minority barcode groups that match a top barcode in a neighbouring cell.

Every top barcode tied by read count is retained. A group is flagged only
when its read count is strictly below the maximum in the same cell and
its barcode is a top barcode in a supplied neighbouring cell. The input
groups and neighbour pairs may be in any order. Inputs are not changed.

:param cell: one integer cell identifier per unique cell/barcode group.
:param barcode: one barcode identifier per group, as strings or codes.
:param reads: the exact plus corrected read count of every group.
:param neighbours: integer cell/neighbour pairs with shape ``(P, 2)``;
    include both orders for an undirected relation, or None for no pairs.
:returns: one boolean flag per input group, in the original group order.
:raises ValueError: when group arrays or nonempty pairs have inconsistent shapes.

spacr.ops_sbs.vote_mapped_reads.before:
Each object's guide from its reads, matched to the library first.

Every read is matched (:class:`LibraryMatcher`); a read at distance one
or more counts only when ``runner_up_margin`` is given and
:func:`runner_up_consistent` passes. The matched reads vote, each with
weight one, or with ``min(1, quality) + weight_floor`` when
``quality_weighted``. An object takes the top guide when it holds at
least ``min_fraction`` of the votes with no tie, and, when one read is
all that supports it, that read's quality reaches
``single_read_quality``.

:param objects: one object id per read.
:param barcodes: one called barcode per read.
:param quality: one quality per read, the worst cycle's margin.
:param data: ``(N, cycles, channels)``, the intensities called from.
:param margin: ``(N, cycles)``, the per-cycle margins.
:param matcher: the guides, and any decoys, to match against.
:param max_distance: the most mismatches a read may carry.
:param runner_up_margin: the runner-up rule's margin, or None to count
    every match within ``max_distance``.
:param quality_weighted: weight votes by read quality.
:param weight_floor: added to every quality weight.
:param min_fraction: the share of the votes the guide must hold.
:param single_read_quality: the quality a one-read guide needs.
:param impute_missing: let an ``N`` -- a cycle that was not measured --
    match any base; False leaves such reads unmatched.
:param strength: one spot strength per read, for the evidence; None
    records none.
:param evidence: a dict filled with the per-object, per-guide tallies
    behind every vote -- ``votes``, ``exact``, ``corrected``, ``best``,
    ``qualities``, ``strength`` and ``matched`` -- for objects assigned
    or not; None keeps none.

Share transient notice state across shallow settings copies in one run.

The context remains private; only the applied flags are published. An
open journal owns a fresh context, so replay metadata never suppresses
the first notice of a new run. Plain API callers share their mutable
settings context across wells without a global process cache.

Record actual discount availability and emit one translated no-op notice per path.

False remains false when one path includes fields without the required
positions. The current journal receives only JSON application flags;
transient notice bookkeeping is never published. A supplied rule-state
mapping preserves notice deduplication during direct cache replays.

Give a file the defaults of the version it was written under.

WHY (item 931). A saved settings file or run journal must give the same
result when it is run again, but a file only holds the keys that existed
when it was written. When a later release changes a default, a key the
file never set would silently take the NEW default. Every file spaCR
writes therefore carries ``SETTINGS_VERSION_KEY`` =
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION``, and ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` says, per version,
what a key's default was BEFORE that version. A file with no stamp --
hand-written or older than the stamp -- is read as the oldest version
and gets every old default listed, with a logged notice naming each one
and how to take today's default instead.

TO CHANGE A DEFAULT: add one row to ``DEFAULT_CHANGES``, keyed by the
item number that changes it and holding the OLD default, and raise
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION`` to that number. The key must be above every
existing key, because files are already stamped with the current
version; an item whose number is lower takes the next free number and
is listed under that number in docs/source/reproducibility_manifests.rst.
A format-only change instead adds its version to
``SETTINGS_FORMAT_VERSIONS`` and leaves ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` unchanged.
Version 950 records exact resolved parameters without changing defaults.
933 is item 930's switch of ``ops_align_model`` to ``'tile_affine'``:
it landed after 932, so it could not take 930. 934 is item 937's
``aggregation_defaults`` ``'per_feature'`` (the screen pipeline's
per-feature well table); older files keep ``'legacy'``.
935 is item 940's switch of ``ops_placement_seed_export`` to True: every
solved stitch writes a placement file, and files stamped before keep
it off.
936 is the OPS stage-3 Hybrid profile's ``ops_blas_threads`` (2, was
1) and ``ops_consensus_space`` (``'hybrid'``, was ``'refit'``).
937 is item 941's removal of Gabor and colocalisation from the
``'profiling'`` preset of ``profile_features`` and
``ops_ph_profile_features``: files stamped before get
``profile_optional_families`` and ``ops_ph_profile_optional_families``
with the three families ``'profiling'`` measured then, so their columns
are unchanged.
938 is item 945's ``seg_mask_vram_gb``: the
large-site mask step is sized to 6 GB of card memory, and files stamped
before keep 0, no cap of its own.
940 is item 946's switch of the OPS decode to the proven Funk decode:

existing key, because files are already stamped with the current
version; an item whose number is lower takes the next free number and
is listed under that number in docs/source/reproducibility_manifests.rst.

``SETTINGS_FORMAT_VERSIONS`` and leaves ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` unchanged.
